event.summary: Race tests use one yield as proof that stale detach arbitration ran
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: the new takeover regression tests may finish their survival assertions before the stale teardown they intend to exercise has actually run, leaving a regression undetected. Source basis: a_stall_teardown_racing_a_takeover_never_detaches_the_winner and takeover_reason_wins_over_a_held_natural_detach use one tokio::task::yield_now before inspecting the attachment, with comments claiming this establishes teardown order. Checks made: read the complete assigned patch; caller/arbiter and executor contracts remain to be inspected. Exact missing premise: whether a finished forwarder plus FIFO lock ordering or delete-over notification actually guarantees the spawned teardown has queued or executed before assertions. Next source checks: inspect pinned connection report_forwarder_end, detach_stalled, detach_naturally, delete_over, test macro/runtime, and governing specs. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage); could-be-highest: false, no product harm route established. Confidence: unresolved lead, not a finding. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: One-yield teardown synchronization has no established failure in this fixture
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR considered: the takeover regression tests could finish survival assertions before stale detach arbitration, missing an attachment-removal regression. Source checks: connection.rs:1272-1326 synchronously spawns the arbiter before GridSender::run returns (grid_stream.rs:936-963); connection.rs:1435-1466 and :1496-1517 have no await before their attachment-lock claim apart from the deliberate delete_over gate; core.rs:851-908 shows dropping the delete mark wakes the natural arbiter. Test macro defaults to a current-thread runtime. Cargo.lock pins Tokio 1.53.2; its task/yield_now.rs uses context::defer, and runtime/scheduler/current_thread/mod.rs:816-887 runs ready tasks before park_yield wakes deferred root futures (:465-476). In the small isolated fixture these give the spawned/woken arbiters a run to the lock; attachment inspection, loser round-trip and later winner output also exercise progress. The stall test checks its intended ordering independently with the loser's exact TakenOver notice, rather than silently passing when the stall wins. Decision: no concrete false-pass or current failure route established from source; do not report a general scheduler-contract hardening suggestion as a defect. Caveat: Tokio's yield_now public docs explicitly disclaim general scheduling-order guarantees, so an explicit arbiter-completion oracle would be stronger under a changed scheduler; this is not evidence of present behavior. Original suspected consequence is preserved above. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage). could-be-highest: false. Confidence: candidate set aside after source investigation, no execution performed. proposed_drop: source analysis above did not substantiate a defect. possible_cover: none.

event.summary: TakenOver notice alone does not witness stale teardown arbitration
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Synthesis correction to the previous candidate: the exact TakenOver notice at host_terminals.rs:3785-3790 establishes the takeover won removal of the old attachment; it does not independently prove the old stall arbiter subsequently claimed the lock, inspected the replacement, or completed. A ListSessions round trip orders frames already enqueued on that connection, not a separate unjoined arbiter. Original suspected consequence remains a regression test passing before stale teardown has a chance to remove the winner. The current source and public yield_now contract are distinct: weak public scheduler guarantees alone do not establish a present failure under pinned Tokio 1.53.2. Checks made this turn: reread complete log; read exact race assertions :3735-3803; testtrace/lib.rs:994-1013 runs the body as runtime.block_on's root future and drops its runtime afterwards. Next checks: exact pinned current-thread deferred-wake scheduling, root wake state and FIFO attachment-lock interaction; natural-detach gate wake and exact assertions; confirm cross-commit c2 behavior is unchanged. Suggested bucket: other; could-be-highest: false. Confidence: reopened source-check lead, not a demonstrated failure. proposed_drop: false while checking the narrower premise. possible_cover: none. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Takeover notice is an ordering check, not a stale-arbiter completion oracle
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. Original TLDR considered: regression tests might finish before stale teardown arbitration and miss the removal of the winning viewer. Synthesis result: no present false-pass or failure is established, but narrow the prior refutation: TakenOver alone never proves the stale arbiter ran. handlers.rs:1822-1879 removes and joins the loser and queues that notice before installing the winner (:1903-1939); connection.rs:1435-1466 and :1496-1517 run separate, unjoined arbiters. host_terminals.rs:3785-3790 therefore checks which path first removed the loser, not whether the stale stall path subsequently completed. The natural test's notice is earlier still (:4008-4018), while the delete mark is held. ListSessions round trips drain earlier queued frames; they do not join these arbiters. Source premises actually established: verdict_reported (:3627-3638), together with grid_stream.rs:936-963 and connection.rs:1272-1326, proves the old output task already spawned its arbiter; the stall test holds attachments until after its yield (:3755-3768), so an arbiter that has polled its lock must queue there. Mutex FIFO then orders it before the test's next lock. The natural arbiter waits in core.rs:898-908; dropping the mark closes its sole sender (:851-867), making it runnable, with no additional external-I/O wait before its attachment-lock claim (connection.rs:1502-1508). Pinned execution model checked this turn: Cargo.lock uses Tokio 1.53.2; testtrace/lib.rs:994-1013 runs the test body as runtime.block_on's root future; :1126-1142 builds an ordinary current-thread runtime. Tokio task/yield_now.rs defers the root waker. Its current_thread scheduler pushes local ready tasks FIFO (:339-362 and :709-738), polls scheduled tasks before returning to the root (:816-880), and wakes deferred wakers on a driver turn (:465-476). The normal event interval is 61 (runtime/builder.rs:262-268), so it is inaccurate to generalize this as an unconditional drain of every ready task before resuming the root: a driver turn can also occur at the interval. This concrete mechanism supports the small fixture's intended run-to-lock ordering; it is not a public completion guarantee and the notice does not replace it. Public yield_now docs explicitly allow the yielding task to be polled again before other tasks and permit scheduler-order changes. Decision: retain as a candidate hardening concern, not a present defect; no pinned-fixture ordering was established in which the tests complete their checks before the runnable stale arbiter can execute. An explicit arbiter-completion/queued-at-lock oracle would remove the private-scheduler dependency, but the weaker public contract alone is not evidence of a current failure. Original consequence preserved above. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage); could-be-highest: false. Confidence: source-only candidate after completed checks, not observed behavior. proposed_drop: no present defect substantiated; prior independent-notice-completion rationale expressly withdrawn and replaced by the narrower analysis above. possible_cover: none. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: TerminalProbe simplification preserves protection against signaling recycled pids
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR considered: deleting TerminalProcess and its stale-pid documentation might let Stop, Restart or tab cleanup kill an unrelated process after a terminal child exits. Source refutation: terminal_process.rs:14-43 carries a pid only in Running and live_pid returns None for Dead and Gone. hosts/terminal.rs:791-832 rechecks the pinned child process start identity before returning Running and treats unreadability as an error; :2557-2583 takes the sweep root from the same pinned identity and rejects a different pid. handlers.rs:865-909 refuses failed probes and obtains sweep_root before recording the stop; core.rs:12377-12397 does the same for Restart; core.rs:14128-14139 roots a tab reap only from Running through sweep_root. Prompt delivery requires Running (core.rs:11944-11958); guarded Delete refuses Running and propagates probe errors (core.rs:13325-13337). The removed foreign-owner result was for the retired tmux backend; no current probe producer needs it, and SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, The terminal switch points states that the supervisor serves no other kind of terminal. Governing runtime contract: SPEC_impl.md Terminal host, A host terminal's runtime says the child is a kill root only while its reported-alive pid has the adoption-pinned start identity, re-read each time. Decision: source refutes the suspected stale-pid regression; retain the candidate for the caller's independent check because the originally considered consequence could be highest. Suggested bucket if true: highest (loss of unrelated user processes). could-be-highest: true. Confidence: confirmed source refutation; no execution performed. proposed_drop: source refutation at the references above, not rarity or specification acceptance alone. possible_cover: none.

event.summary: GridPeer channel bookkeeping does not skip a new catch-up in assigned callers
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR considered: splitting attach submission from its reply while retaining per-channel replay/detach flags could let a test skip a replacement attachment's catch-up using an old channel's ReplayComplete, hiding a broken new stream. Source check/result: read GridPeer implementation and searched every attach, attach_session and attach_reply call in the pinned host_terminals.rs. All successful attachments use a fresh peer/channel state. The sole same-peer channel-1 retry at :3510 and :3534 follows an Unavailable refusal, not an earlier successful attachment, so it has neither an old client nor a recorded ReplayComplete to reuse. The two successful attachments on one peer at :3896-3903 use distinct channels 1 and 2. Takeover-race tests use distinct loser and winner peers; send_attach/attach_reply on the winner is one successful attach, not a replacement of its own previous one. Thus no assigned caller exercises the suspected stale-cache route; :3327-3330 installs the new client before subsequent frames are read. Decision: source-refuted for the assigned patch/callers; no new defect. Suggested bucket if true: other (test oracle). could-be-highest: false; no product security/work-loss route. Confidence: source-only caller refutation. proposed_drop: exact caller analysis above, not production correctness or specification acceptance. possible_cover: none. Caveat: GridPeer is not a general reusable-channel test driver and would need per-attachment bookkeeping reset if a future test attaches twice successfully on its own same channel; that hypothetical future use is not a finding. No execution or reproduction performed.
